name: Badge
summary: Mark a role, a flag or a count with a small passive label.

useWhen: Marking an item with a short role, flag or count that the user reads and does not act on.
avoidWhen: A set of labels the user selects or removes; use TagGroup.
A notice about the whole page; use Toast.
An action or a link; use Button.

obligations: A Badge is passive text: it has no role, takes no focus stop and does nothing when pressed.
Its visible text says what it means; the tone never carries meaning alone, and under forced colours every badge is CanvasText with a CanvasText edge.
When the visible text is not enough, such as a bare count, label gives the words assistive technology reads in its place; inside a link they become part of the link's name.
The icon is decorative and hidden from assistive technology, so a badge whose only content is an icon needs a label.

behavior: Badge is a span with no role. It passes its native span attributes on, except role and tabIndex, so it never becomes a focus stop or a control.
tone is neutral, brand, success, warning or error, the semantic tones of TagGroup, and variant is soft or solid; another value throws a TypeError.
Soft paints the tone's weak tint and the soft tag's text and solid the selected tag's fill and text from TagGroup's tone tokens, so a theme that changes those tones changes Badge too.
With a label, the visible text is hidden from assistive technology and the label is read in its place, as visually hidden text inside the badge.
The text keeps to one line and ends in an ellipsis when the badge is narrower than it; numbers use tabular figures.
